failure_summary.description: The agent returned a salient detail instead of the requested referent or property, despite existing rules to identify the answer slot and honor the clue’s scope.
Flattened trivia metadata, bare character lists, and compact wordplay clues lacked specific guidance for recovering the intended answer.
The answers used a different name form from the expected canonical form, including an expanded company name and a familiar nickname.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers identifying the requested referent and respecting clue scope, so those failures are noted as ignored rules rather than duplicated. The edits add guidance for three clue formats not addressed explicitly and reinforce the distinction between an explicitly requested measurement and a correlated attribute.

edits.content: For flattened trivia prompts, clue text, category labels, and answer-length markers may run together without punctuation. Use context to identify category or length metadata (including a trailing label and parenthetical number), and solve the clue itself rather than returning the category label.

When a prompt is only a list of character names or roles, use context to identify their shared work or program if that is the implied target. Return the work or program, not the performers, unless the prompt asks for the cast.

For compact definition or wordplay clues that give two linked readings, solve the whole clue for the conventional term satisfying both; do not merely restate one reading. Preserve an article when it is part of the expected expression.

Honor the measurement or attribute explicitly requested: for example, “smallest in size” asks about physical dimensions, not denomination or value. Do not substitute a related property for the stated one; use evidence about the requested property.
